dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The user's stated 7-beat flow spans three tools (ideation, OpenSpec, superpowers) and four-plus sessions with nothing computing where the work stands; the model-routing commands that partially solve it (~/.claude/commands/spec/*.md) were found to be in no git repo at all.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Four measurable goals fixed in interview: correct stage named at 7/7 beats, model+effort sourced from a manifest for 100% of stages, provider swap costs exactly 1 file edit and 0 wrapper edits, and the worktree beat reduced to 1 command.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Eight criteria carry runnable commands with positive twins (fixture-count anchor, no-hardcoded-model grep, one-file-diff swap assertion, zero-dependency probe) and one is an explicit judgment call naming which beats required a lookup.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: v1 is status/next/start plus provider manifests; --auto drive mode is explicitly deferred to v2; the inner TDD loop, merge mechanics, and the interview itself are explicitly owned by existing tools and excluded.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The one tension found -- 'no state file' versus 'every stage is pluggable', since inference facts are provider-specific -- was resolved by moving the detector into the provider manifest so it swaps atomically with the command.

problem: A single change moves through seven beats -- rough ideation, branch and worktree, refined ideation, contract, specs, execute specs 1..n, cleanup -- spanning three separate tool ecosystems and at least four Claude sessions. No tool models the arc. Each session boundary costs a manual re-orientation: which stage is this, which command comes next, which model does it want, and does the work live in the main checkout or a worktree.

Two beats are modeled by nothing at all. The branch-and-worktree moment, which the user's own AGENTS.md mandates for feature work, is invoked by no planning tool -- gwt is a zsh function nothing calls. And no command ends by naming its successor, so the baton is carried in the user's head across a /clear that deliberately erases everything else.

The partial fix already in place is unmanaged and fragile: ~/.claude/commands/spec/{explore,propose,apply,archive}.md encode which model runs which stage, and they exist in no git repository -- one disk failure from gone, and unreproducible on a second machine.
goals: At each of the 7 beats, one command names the current stage, the next command, and the model plus effort it wants -- zero notes consulted, zero recall required.
100% of stages source their model and effort from a declarative provider manifest rather than from the operator's memory.
Replacing the tool bound to any pluggable stage costs exactly 1 manifest file edit and 0 edits to Pitwall itself.
The branch-and-worktree beat reduces to a single command that is idempotent and correct from either the main checkout or an existing worktree.

successCriteria.criterion: Stage inference resolves the correct beat from repository reality at all 7 beats, including mid-execute n-of-N progress.
The baton names the command, model, and effort declared in that stage's provider manifest, and no model name is hardcoded anywhere in Pitwall's source.

check.cmd: node --test tests/baton.test.js && grep -rqE '(opus|sonnet|haiku)' providers/ && ! grep -rqE '(opus|sonnet|haiku)' src/

successCriteria.criterion: Swapping a provider costs exactly one manifest file edit and zero edits to Pitwall's source: the swap fixture asserts a working-tree diff of exactly 1 path, under providers/.
The worktree beat creates one worktree at the sibling-path convention, is idempotent on re-run, is a no-op inside the target worktree, and falls back correctly when the repo has no origin remote.

The gitignore preflight detects every workflow artifact path that git check-ignore matches in the host repo and stays silent on a clean repo (fixture pair: ignored must be reported, clean must be silent).
Every declared command file exists and parses, and the plugin manifest lists exactly the shipped commands.
Pitwall ships zero third-party npm runtime dependencies and needs no build step (external CLIs are a separate, declared category and are stubbed in fixtures).
The full self-test suite passes from a clean checkout.
One real change is driven root-to-merged-PR through Pitwall; the operator lists which of the 7 beats, if any, required consulting notes.

check.judgment: Operator runs a real change end to end and names the beats that required a lookup; pass at zero beats.

mvp.item: Stage inference core -- derive the current beat from git state, worktree presence, and provider detectors
mvp.reason: Every other feature renders this; it is what replaces the rejected state file.

mvp.item: Provider manifests: markdown with flat scalar-only frontmatter, body used verbatim as baton text, and a bounded two-key detector (doneWhenPathExists glob, optional doneWhenCmd judged by exit code)
mvp.reason: The detector must swap with the provider; bounding it declaratively prevents an expression evaluator growing inside a data file.

mvp.item: /pitwall:next -- one surface printing current beat, completed beats, n-of-N execute progress, and the baton (command, model, effort, whether to /clear)
mvp.reason: Goal 1 names one command; a second rendering of the same inference result is traced to no goal.

mvp.item: /pitwall:start -- branch and worktree creation at the direction-known beat
mvp.reason: The beat no existing tool models, and the anchor that lets inference locate later artifacts.

mvp.item: Gitignore preflight -- report every workflow artifact path that git check-ignore matches in the host repo
mvp.reason: Untracked artifacts die when /mar removes the worktree; this makes the host-repo hazard a product feature instead of an untestable assertion.

mvp.item: Cleanup baton to a manifest-configured target (default /mar)
mvp.reason: Goal 1 claims 7/7 beats, so the seventh cannot sit in a later tier; /mar is a personal dotfile, so the target must be declarative.

mvp.item: Built-in provider manifests for ideation and OpenSpec
mvp.reason: One manifest per pluggable stage is what day-one operation needs.

mvp.item: Self-test suite over temp-repo fixtures frozen at each of the 7 beats
mvp.reason: User-chosen mechanical gate; what makes the inference safe to refactor.

full.reason: Promote only if the combined /pitwall:next output proves too dense in the acceptance run.

full.item: superpowers provider manifest for the execute beat
full.reason: A second binding for an already-bound stage; it becomes the first real exercise of the 1-file-edit swap.

full.item: Vendor the four unmanaged ~/.claude/commands/spec/*.md into version control
full.reason: The OpenSpec manifest emits batons pointing at files that exist in no git repo -- the problem statement's own third defect.

full.item: Packaging as a github-sourced plugin registered in the tinetti marketplace
full.reason: Matches how ideation is installed; makes a second machine a one-line install.
The most-used commands are typed many times per change.

full.item: README and install docs naming external prerequisites (openspec CLI, /mar, gh)
full.reason: A standalone repo with undeclared prerequisites is unusable on a second machine.

outOfScope.item: The inner TDD / implement / review loop
outOfScope.reason: OpenSpec apply and superpowers already own it; duplicating it would make Pitwall a competitor rather than a spine.
/mar already does this well; Pitwall hands off to it.
ideation's evidence gates and plan critics are better than anything this project would produce.

outOfScope.item: Any persisted state file for workflow position
outOfScope.reason: Explicitly rejected -- a second source of truth drifts the first time a stage is done by hand.
The stage model is built on git and spec artifacts; generalizing now would dilute v1.
Inference from repository reality is already machine-independent; nothing to sync.
The preflight reports the hazard; un-ignoring someone's repo is their call, and one-shot remediations belong in phase notes.

future: --auto drive mode: tmux window plus claude --model <m> -p per stage — Feasibility confirmed (claude CLI exposes --model, -p, --fork-session) but it is the riskiest surface and the half used least.
Append-only handoff notes file per change — Carries decisions and dead ends across sessions; inference does not need it, so it is additive.

decisions.decision: Build a thin wrapper with pluggable provider holes
decisions.rejected: Adopt OpenSpec or ideation wholesale as the workflow spine
decisions.reason: Neither models the worktree beat, per-stage model routing, or the session baton; binding the workflow to one tool makes replacing that tool a rewrite rather than a config edit.

decisions.decision: Hybrid authority -- direct (baton) by default, drive (--auto) available later
decisions.rejected: A pure orchestrator that launches every session itself
decisions.reason: Baton mode is the half used every day and needs no new infrastructure; a session launcher is the piece most likely to need iteration and the piece whose crashes the operator must debug.

decisions.decision: Infer stage from repository reality; ship no state file
decisions.rejected: A .pitwall/state.json recording stage, providers, and history
decisions.reason: A second source of truth drifts the moment a stage is done by hand, and inference stays correct even when the operator bypasses the wrapper entirely.

decisions.decision: Each provider manifest carries its own done-detector
decisions.rejected: Pitwall hardcodes detectors for the tools it knows about
decisions.reason: Inference facts are provider-specific (contract-data.json implies ideation); a hardcoded detector would make 'every stage is a hole' false, since swapping a provider would silently break stage resolution.

decisions.decision: Pitwall owns the worktree beat and the cleanup handoff outright
decisions.rejected: Making worktree and cleanup pluggable like the other stages
decisions.reason: They are the two beats no existing tool models, and the worktree is the anchor that lets inference locate every later artifact -- pluggable anchors cannot be relied on.

decisions.decision: One baton per spec/phase during execute
decisions.rejected: One baton for the whole execute stage; one baton per task
decisions.reason: A phase is roughly one session's worth of context; whole-stage cannot report 3-of-9 progress, and per-task churns sessions for a 10+ item tasks.md.

decisions.decision: v1 ships baton mode and the worktree beat; --auto is deferred
decisions.rejected: Shipping drive mode in v1
decisions.reason: The inference model is the load-bearing idea and must be proven before a session launcher is layered on top of it.

decisions.decision: A self-test recipe over temp-repo fixtures is the mechanical gate
decisions.rejected: No pre-check (the real run is the test); manual dry-run only
decisions.reason: A broken detector would otherwise surface mid-change, and fixtures are what make the inference safe to refactor later.

decisions.decision: Standalone repo tinetti/pitwall, registered in the marketplace as a github-sourced plugin
decisions.rejected: plugins/pitwall in the claude-plugins marketplace; files/home/.claude in tinetti_dev_tools
decisions.reason: Cleanest boundary and independent versioning; a marketplace-sibling worktree would land inside the directory Claude Code scans for marketplaces.

decisions.decision: Name it Pitwall, with pw as the short alias
decisions.rejected: wot, stint, pacenote
decisions.reason: The pit wall calls strategy and decides who drives what and when, which is exactly the model-routing and stage-sequencing role; wot and stint were considered and set aside after direct comparison.

decisions.decision: Workflow artifacts must be tracked in git, not gitignored
decisions.rejected: Leaving openspec/ and ideation docs ignored as they are today in tinetti_dev_tools
decisions.reason: Untracked files do not travel to a new worktree and are destroyed when /mar removes it, so the change folder would vanish at exactly the moment the PR needs it.

decisions.decision: Zero third-party runtime dependencies; node --test as the harness
decisions.rejected: A test framework plus a YAML library
decisions.reason: A workflow tool that must run in any repo on any machine cannot carry an install step; frontmatter parsing is small enough to own.

decisions.decision: Provider manifests are markdown with flat scalar-only frontmatter; the parser is capped at key: value and the body is the baton text
decisions.rejected: General YAML (library or hand-rolled) and pure JSON manifests
decisions.reason: Critic showed nothing outside Pitwall's loader reads these files, so the md+frontmatter 'idiom' argument buys only familiarity -- but the body doubling as baton prose earns the markdown; capping the parser removes the YAML edge cases from the blocking phase.

decisions.decision: Detectors are two declarative keys judged by path glob or exit code
decisions.rejected: Arbitrary predicate logic or shell-eval inside the manifest
decisions.reason: An unbounded detector is a plugin execution runtime no goal asks for; goal 3 only needs the detector to swap with its provider.

decisions.decision: One command surface: /pitwall:next prints position and baton together
decisions.rejected: Shipping /pitwall:status as a separate MVP command
decisions.reason: Two lenses independently found status traced to no goal and covered by no criterion, while duplicating rendering, alias, manifest and README surface.

decisions.decision: The openspec CLI is a declared external dependency with a tasks.md checkbox fallback detector
decisions.rejected: Treating openspec status --json as ambiently available
decisions.reason: It appeared in phase notes but in no goal, scope item, or prereq, and it silently contradicted the zero-dependency claim; the JSON shape is unverified, so a fallback is required.

decisions.decision: Worktree path resolution (findMainWorktree, resolveWorktreePath) lands in phase 1, consumed by both inference and the worktree command
decisions.rejected: Phases 2 and 4 running parallel with the sibling-path derivation living in phase 4
decisions.reason: The contract calls the worktree the anchor for inference, so phase 2's detectors need the derivation phase 4 was going to implement -- a circular dependency declared as parallelism.

decisions.decision: The gitignore hazard becomes a shipped preflight, not an acceptance assertion
decisions.rejected: tests/artifacts-tracked.test.js as the check for artifact tracking
decisions.reason: It asserts a host-repo property that Pitwall's own fixtures cannot observe -- a git init fixture with no .gitignore passes for free while the real repo still loses the change folder.

decisions.decision: The cleanup baton ships in MVP with a manifest-configured target defaulting to /mar
decisions.rejected: Cleanup in the Full tier with /mar hardcoded
decisions.reason: Goal 1 claims 7/7 beats so the seventh cannot sit in a later tier, and /mar is a personal dotfile pair plus gh/jq -- installing the plugin alone would emit a baton to a command that does not exist.

decisions.decision: MVP ships two built-in manifests (ideation, OpenSpec); superpowers moves to Full
decisions.rejected: Three built-in manifests in MVP
decisions.reason: superpowers is a second candidate for an already-bound beat; deferring it makes it the first real test of the one-file-edit swap promise.

phases.title: Scaffold, manifest format, and repo-shape helpers
phases.notes: package.json with engines.node (no dependencies, no build script), capped flat-frontmatter parser, provider manifest schema + loader with bounded detectors, findMainWorktree/resolveWorktreePath helpers consumed by phases 2 and 4, and a capability probe verifying openspec status --json exists and recording the field names inference reads. No plugin.json here -- packaging is phase 5. Write phase 2's fixtures directly rather than designing a shared harness up front.

phases.title: Stage inference core
prereqs: Scaffold, manifest format, and repo-shape helpers
phases.notes: Resolve the current beat from git state, worktree presence, and provider detectors; n-of-N execute progress via openspec status --json with a tasks.md checkbox fallback when the CLI is absent. Ships the built-in ideation and OpenSpec manifests. The load-bearing phase.

phases.title: Baton command and gitignore preflight
phases.notes: /pitwall:next renders position plus baton with model/effort routing sourced only from manifests; gitignore preflight surfaces artifact paths matched by git check-ignore. Parallel with phase 4.

phases.title: Worktree beat
phases.notes: /pitwall:start using phase 1's path helpers. Reference implementation is files/zsh/git.zsh:267-288 in tinetti_dev_tools, which assumes an origin remote and origin/<default> base -- specify the remote-less fallback (base = current HEAD, skip fetch). Idempotent, and a no-op inside the target worktree. Parallel with phase 3.

phases.title: Cleanup baton, packaging, and adoption
phases.notes: Cleanup baton to the manifest-configured target; vendor the four unmanaged spec/*.md commands; pw alias; README naming external prerequisites. Packaging prereqs: create and push github.com/tinetti/pitwall (the local repo has no origin and no commits), then clone tinetti/claude-plugins and hand-write a github-sourced entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json -- sync-marketplace.ts preserves object-source entries rather than generating them. One-time: un-ignore openspec/ in tinetti_dev_tools before the acceptance run.
